title: Effects of a Virtual Reality Headset during Outpatient Breast Surgery under Tumescent Local Anesthesia on Pain - A Prospective Randomized Study
summary:
Medications for pain and anxiety during surgery can cause side effects and are often time-consuming and costly. A promising alternative is the use of a virtual reality headset (VR headset), which directs the patient's attention to a relaxing scenario, thereby reducing the perception of pain.
At the Department of Gynecology in Tübingen, breast surgeries have been routinely performed under local anesthesia without general anesthesia since 2022. During the procedure, the patient lies on the operating table and is shielded from the surgical field by a sterile drape. In this situation, a VR headset with calming scenarios (e.g., a beach walk or a journey through space) can be specifically used for distraction and relaxation.
This randomized study investigates whether the use of the HypnoVR® VR headset during surgery reduces pain, anxiety, and stress, and improves patient satisfaction. In addition, medical staff will also be surveyed regarding their satisfaction with the use of the VR headset.
conditions: Neoplasm of uncertain or unknown behaviour: Breast
Other signs and symptoms in breast

interventions.name: Intervention group: Patients undergoing outpatient breast surgery under tumescent local anesthesia wearing the CE-marked VR headset HypnoVR®.
Control group: Patients undergoing the same procedure without the use of a VR headset.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Sufficient German language skills (spoken and written) for independent communication and understanding of the study information and informed consent form
Written informed consent after explanation
No contraindication to local anesthetic
Planned outpatient breast surgery under tumescent local anesthesia
Exclusion criteria:
Insufficient German language skills (spoken and written) preventing understanding of the study information or the provision of informed consent
Missing patient consent
Expected lack of compliance or inability of the patient to understand the purpose and objectives of the clinical trial
Needle phobia or claustrophobia
Advanced dementia or cognitive impairment (clinical assessment: inability to provide informed consent or follow instructions)
Pregnancy
Pre-existing neurological conditions (migraine, epilepsy, known motion sickness)
Eye conditions that significantly impair the use of the VR headset (e.g., advanced macular degeneration, severe cataract)
Positional vertigo
